# Native screen outline diagnostic

Original rectangles and ellipses, no text or external artwork, generated by
`tools/outline_display_width_fixture.py` and
`tools/outline_display_holdouts_fixture.py`. The first generator uses the
repository's independently authored thin-outline OPC fixture. The second adds
rounding, fractional-position and group controls. ZIP entry contents reproduce
exactly; ZIP timestamps are not the reproducibility contract.

## Sources

- `legacy.docx`: eight widths, each on a rectangle and ellipse, without an
  explicit compatibility-mode setting. Browser diagnostic only.
- `modern.docx`: the same sixteen shapes with compatibility mode 15. Widths
  are 0, 1588, 3175, 4327, 6350, 9525, 12700 and 19050 EMUs.
- `rounding.docx`: widths near 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 screen pixels at 100% zoom.
  Inspect the integer EMU values in the case manifest: rounding a requested
  half-pixel width to EMUs can put it just above or below the midpoint.
- `phase.docx`: one-pixel pens with successive fractional-pixel positions.
- `group-phase.docx`: those same shapes as children of one drawing group.
- `group-widths.docx`: the modern widths inside a group whose coordinate
  transform scales by two. Child frames are halved so final geometry is equal.

## Native capture protocol

Open private copies through the reference-application document helper and
confirm the exact path. Use the native Zoom dialog
to capture `modern` at 50%, 100% and 200%; capture the other four native controls
at 100%. Move the pointer outside the artwork before capturing. The captures
are produced with Sky `get_window_state`; its returned screenshot pixels are
saved for measurement. Do not resize the captures. Save no document edits.

`reference.json` records the observed page origins, private full-capture
hashes, fixture/native-source hashes, matching package-entry hashes, measured
cross-sections and browser baseline observations. `word-*.png` are unscaled
analytical crops of the generated page, excluding application chrome. `app-*.png`
are complete canvas images at browser device scale 1. The native caret/page
border are outside all measured shape regions.

`native-modern.pdf` is the reference application's fixed-format export of that same private modern
source. Its sixteen stroked paths use widths
`.14, .14, .14, .14, .25, .25, .34071, .34071, .5, .5, .75, .75, 1, 1, 1.5, 1.5`
points. The already documented .14-point physical floor is distinct from the
screen behavior measured here.

## Findings and limits

All **56 rectangular cross-sections** match a minimum of one captured screen
pixel and nearest-integer rounding of the authored pixel width. Widths just
below/above 1.5 pixels produce one/two pixels; those below/above 2.5 produce
two/three. The 2× group transform does not multiply the pen. Fractional top and
left edges in both ungrouped and grouped controls land at the nearest pixel.

The 220 red-channel threshold in the recorder separates the opaque C0C0C0
straight-edge stroke from faint capture ringing. It is a measurement technique,
not an opacity correction or a rendering rule. The stored profiles expose the
actual values. Ellipses are included as visual references, but these assertions
do not certify their curved pixels. Other DPRs, rotations, custom curves,
transparent strokes, compound lines, dashes, markers and effects still need
controls before a general display implementation can be claimed complete.

The browser renders some thin pens extremely faintly or omits their sampled
cross-section at reduced zoom. The supplied planner #226 has 474 .34071-point
outlines; this display behavior explains an additional failure beyond the
previous PDF-based curve coverage investigation. It does not prove that the
entire planner mismatch has a single cause.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses are 20.1.2.2.24 (`ln`) and 20.1.10.35
(`ST_LineWidth`). They specify physical widths in EMUs, not a screen-pixel
snapping algorithm. This records a reference display-compatibility requirement,
not a claim that those clauses prohibit the reference application's rasterization. Changing the
stored widths to screen widths would corrupt physical semantics.

**No renderer change or corpus promotion is included.** All six controls import
editable on one page at 50%, 100% and 200% (18 browser captures), and their XML
passes 23 standard/extension schema views. The evidence directs the next fix
to display-space pen/geometry handling, with original geometry and package
preservation retained.

## Reproduction

Run both generators with the configured Python runtime. After native capture,
run `node tools/diagnose-outline-display.mjs <private-output-directory>` against
the existing Vite server on port 5173. Its private output directory is named
`outline-display-browser` beneath the native capture directory for the recorder.
Then run `python tools/record_outline_display.py <private-capture-directory>`.
The recorder checks native source/package equivalence, measures the original
captures, creates unscaled page crops and records the PDF pens.

## Reference correction (2026-09-30)

The first 200% capture contained a blue pointer halo over the upper-left
shapes. It did not intersect the recorded rectangle cross-sections, so the
56 width assertions passed while the surrounding curve reference was polluted.
The replacement was captured from the same open, unedited control at 200%,
after moving the pointer to the Home tab and observing a fresh screenshot.
All 56 profiles and the 16 PDF pens remain unchanged; only the 200% screenshot
and crop hashes changed in `reference.json`.

The recorder now rejects non-neutral pixels throughout the measurement region
of **every rectangle and ellipse**, including four pixels of surrounding space.
The previous capture fails this check; all seven current captures pass. This
check is specific to these deliberately grayscale fixtures. It does not prove
absence of neutral overlays such as a caret, nor replace visual inspection.

The planner comparison also needs care: its private live capture includes a
gray reference page edge at the previously used top row. That row is not document
ink and must be excluded from contrast measurements. A one-pixel registration
change materially alters candidate rankings; do not infer a rendering rule by
optimizing screenshot translation. The experimental rounded-pen/path candidates
remain unshipped. Establish curved-path placement and coverage with independent
controls before using these rectangle width observations for a general fix.

## Capture encoding and curve follow-up

The original private `outline-modern-screen-100.png` and `-200.png` files were
inspected by signature: both contain JPEG bytes returned by Sky. The committed
PNG crops preserve decoded JPEG artifacts. “Unscaled” above describes dimensions,
not lossless acquisition. Rectangle threshold measurements retain their stated
scope; raw ink totals cannot establish a curve-coverage or opacity rule.
New [independent curve controls](../outline-curve-display/README.md) retain the
encoding metadata and establish a separate whole-twip anchor-placement mismatch
through the reference application's vector PDF. Rounded screen-pen candidates remain unshipped.
